title: The normalization of a scheme in a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over it
statement:
Let $f:T	o X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then there are a scheme $X'$ and morphisms $
u:X'	o X$, $f':T	o X'$ with $f=
u\circ f'$ (the normalization of $X$ in $T$, $X'=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_X(\mathcal O')$ with $\mathcal O'$ the integral closure of $\mathcal O_X$ in $f_*\mathcal O_T$) such that: (i) $
u$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; (ii) $f'$ is dominant ($f'(T)$ is dense in $X'$); (iii) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $B=\Gamma(f^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_T)$ made an $A$-algebra by $f^\sharp$ and $A'\subseteq B$ the integral closure of $A$ in $B$, the open $
u^{-1}(U)$ is affine and there is a ring isomorphism $	heta_U:\Gamma(
u^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{X'})\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$ under which $
u^\sharp:A	o\Gamma(
u^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{X'})$ becomes the structure map $A	o A'$ and $f'^\sharp:\Gamma(
u^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{X'})	o\Gamma(f^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_T)=B$ becomes the inclusion $A'\subseteq B$; (iv) if $T$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], so is $X'$.
